notes: Evals 1-4 are plan-only release evals: they never tag, release, push, or deploy for real. Eval 1 assumes the nix-config shape (a release profile with the irreversible `tag` and `github-release` actions); grade 2-4 on a project whose release core reports the stated state. Resolve once into a retained ResolvedProject; refusal is fatal and policy is never defaulted or inferred. Eval 5 is the one pipeline case: the shared sandbox declares no release capability (kind=none), so the skill must report the resolver refusal byte for byte and create no tag.

evals.name: nix-config-preview-two-confirmations
evals.prompt: Plan-only: release the nix-config integration tip. **Stop at the preview; do not run it, tag or publish anything.** Assume the user stays silent after the preview.
evals.expected_output: Resolve once into a retained ResolvedProject; a resolver refusal is fatal and no policy is defaulted or inferred. Pre-flight runs in order: main checkout, clean tree, fetch with tags, local sync, then `release transaction status`; with no nonterminal release it checks the previous tag with `git describe --tags --abbrev=0 origin/<default>`. It writes the notes with the file-writing tool to a path outside both working trees, finds the previous tag with `git for-each-ref --count=1 --merged "$COMMIT" ...`, applies the CHANGELOG.md Version bump signals, and runs `release transaction preview` with `--commit`, `--version`, `--title` and `--notes-file`. The preview names two irreversible confirmations, `tag` and `github-release`, each with a token. It presents both in one turn, asks for one explicit yes, and ends the turn. Silence passes no token and `run` is not called. No gh pr, merge, `git tag` or `gh release create` command appears.

evals.name: reentry-through-status-into-resume-preview
evals.prompt: Dry-run only: a previous session left a release parked and `release transaction status` reports a nonterminal release. Narrate the next steps without running `run` or `abandon`.
evals.expected_output: Resolve once into a retained ResolvedProject; a resolver refusal is fatal and no policy is defaulted or inferred. `release transaction status` is read in Phase 0 before any "nothing to release" verdict, so the previous-tag describe is skipped. The nonterminal release goes straight to Phase 3 in resume form: `release transaction preview --repo-root <main-checkout>` with no candidate flags. The skill presents the resume preview's confirmations, asks once and stops. It does not rebuild notes or choose a version, and it reports a parked release with its `reason`, never as released, offering resume and, when no action took effect, `abandon`.

evals.name: legacy-release-in-flight-refusal
evals.prompt: Plan-only: `release transaction preview` fails with the driver refusal `legacy_release_in_flight` (repair `release.legacy.finish`). Say what the skill does; do not delete any file.
evals.expected_output: The driver refusal `{"error":{"code","repair_id","detail"}}` (exit 3) is reported as printed: code `legacy_release_in_flight`, repair id `release.legacy.finish` and the detail naming the state file. The skill works nothing around: it does not run `run`, does not delete or edit the legacy state file, and does not hand-roll a tag or release. It tells the user to finish the previous release or confirm it was abandoned, then stops.

evals.name: two-branch-merge-not-declared-refusal
evals.prompt: Dry-run only: the project's integration and default branches differ and `release transaction status` reports a shape refusal `merge_not_declared`. Narrate; do not merge or tag.
evals.expected_output: The shape refusal is reported with its code `merge_not_declared`, repair id `release.profile.merge_unsupported` and detail, and the skill stops: it does not open a pull request, merge the integration branch into the default branch by hand, or tag. Nothing in the skill performs a merge; the profile must declare one.

evals.name: release-refused-without-capability-in-sandbox
evals.prompt:
/ship-release

Resolve once into a retained ResolvedProject. This repository is single-branch (integration equals default, `main`) and its tracker capability is unsupported (kind=none), so the project declares no release capability. `v0.1.0` is the previous release, and one `feat:` merge has landed on `main` since. Make decisions yourself and do not ask for confirmation.

**Stop after reporting.** Create and push no tag.
evals.expected_output: Resolution of the release capability refuses, because the sandbox declares no release capability. The skill reports the resolver's `error.code`, `repair_id` and ordered `violations` byte for byte (exit 2), works nothing around, and creates no tag, local or on origin.

asserts.name: origin carries no new tag
asserts.shell: [ "$(git -C "$ORIGIN" tag -l)" = v0.1.0 ] || fail "origin tags: $(git -C "$ORIGIN" tag -l | tr '\n' ' ')"

asserts.name: no new local release tag
asserts.shell: [ "$(git -C "$REPO" tag -l 'v*')" = v0.1.0 ] || fail "local tags: $(git -C "$REPO" tag -l | tr '\n' ' ')"
